notes: Client/model behavior is specific to the recorded versions and isolated instruction fixtures; this is not approval to enable v2 for every client.
Completed model turns are separate from account-usage-limit interruptions and unattempted turns. The latter two do not prove either behavioral success or failure.

Version 1 is graded against the target version 2 acceptance rubric for baseline measurement. Claude v1 often put its footer in commentary and ended with a short acknowledgement; strict final-answer failures are preserved and are not a newly introduced v1 regression.
Tool-result byte counts are measured serialized MCP results. They are not tokenizer counts. Paired comparisons use only matching completed model turns.
Latency is wall time per CLI turn, including startup and tool execution. Median and nearest-rank p95 are descriptive measurements, not a controlled causal speed estimate.
Original runs did not capture a scorer hash. The recorded scorer hash identifies the archived regrading implementation; original verdicts remain preserved.
Client-reported numeric usage snapshots are retained per turn. Counters may be cumulative across resumed sessions; snapshots are not summed or presented as token savings.
Raw report, response and tool trace text is kept only in the local ignored archive. This compact artifact excludes raw text, session IDs, home paths and credentials.
Simulated compaction starts a fresh CLI session with an explicitly retained factual summary; it is not a measurement of a client-native compaction algorithm.
